passage:
Dear Sangeeta,

Promise you won't laugh. Ever since Mr Rao started reading poems aloud in English, my stomach does a little flip when he walks in. I sit up straight, I know every answer, and yesterday when he said "good" to me I nearly floated home. It's the best and most embarrassing feeling ever. 😅 I even started a poem for him, then tore it into tiny pieces and put it in the bin under the tissues. Remember you told me about your tuition-sir crush last year, and how it just faded? I'm hanging onto that. I'm not going to give him anything or write him notes. It's mine, and it stays in this letter. Kabir from debate club asked to borrow my notes, so maybe I'll be a bit nicer to him. Tell me it's normal!

Lakshmi

qa.q: What did Lakshmi do with the poem she started for Mr Rao?
qa.a: She tore it into tiny pieces and put it in the bin under the tissues.

qa.q: How does Lakshmi feel about her feelings for Mr Rao, and what shows it?
qa.a: She finds them thrilling but embarrassing. Her stomach flips when he walks in, she nearly floated home after his "good", and she asks Sangeeta not to laugh.

qa.q: What did Lakshmi choose to do about her crush, and why is it a sensible choice?
qa.a: She keeps it private and gives Mr Rao no notes, hoping it fades like Sangeeta's did. That avoids an awkward situation, and she can turn her attention toward classmates her own age.

qa.q: How might Sangeeta feel on reading the letter?
qa.a: Probably fond and understanding, since she had a similar crush that faded. She may also feel trusted, because Lakshmi shares something so private with her.

grounding: The protagonist describes a thrilling crush on a teacher and chooses to keep it private and not act on it.

passage:
Week one. Aadhya's new history teacher, Jatin sir, told stories about ancient cities like he'd lived in them. When he praised her answer, her face went hot for the whole period. She started walking the long way past the staff room.
Week three. She wrote him a long note on pink paper about how he was "the only one who understands." She read it at night, heart racing. In the morning she showed it to her best friend Kritika instead of giving it to him.
Kritika read it and said gently, "This is a real feeling. But he's our teacher. This note could get awkward for everyone. Keep it for yourself."
Aadhya felt embarrassed, then relieved. She tore it up.
Week eight. The feeling had faded to just liking history. At the inter-school quiz, a boy from the other team, Parth, made her laugh during the break. She found herself thinking about him on the bus home instead.

qa.q: What colour paper did Aadhya write the note on?
How did Aadhya feel when Kritika read the note?
qa.a: She felt embarrassed at first, then relieved, realising that keeping the feeling private was safer.
Showing the note to Kritika and tearing it up kept the crush private and avoided an awkward situation with a teacher.

qa.q: How might Kritika see Aadhya's feelings for Jatin sir?
qa.a: Kritika sees them as real but inappropriate to act on, and gently helps Aadhya keep them private.

grounding: A teen develops a crush on a teacher, keeps it private instead of giving a dramatic note, and later finds the feeling fades as she notices a peer.

passage:
Uma, you're blushing every time you mention your English teacher. Sit down, I won't tease you. I'll tell you a secret instead.
When I was sixteen, in Kolkata, I had a huge crush on our geography teacher, Miss Roy. She wore green saris and laughed at our silly questions. I used to rehearse clever things to say to her. I even drew her a map of Bengal with a poem on the back.
That was the turning point, the map. I never gave it to her. I showed it to my elder brother first. He didn't laugh. He said, "It's normal, Arnab. Almost everyone has one crush like this. But she's your teacher. Keep it inside, and it will pass."
It did pass, slowly, by the next year. I still love geography, thanks to her. And by Class 12 I was writing much worse poems for a girl from my tuition.
So enjoy the feeling, but keep it to yourself. That's what your Arnab Mama learned.

qa.q: What did young Arnab draw for Miss Roy?
qa.a: A map of Bengal with a poem on the back.

qa.q: How did young Arnab feel about Miss Roy?
qa.a: He felt thrilled and infatuated, rehearsing clever things to say and wanting to impress her.

qa.q: What was the turning point, and why was it wise?
qa.a: Arnab showed the map to his brother instead of giving it to Miss Roy, and kept the crush private until it passed.

qa.q: How might Miss Roy have felt if she had received the map and poem?
qa.a: Miss Roy would likely have felt awkward and had to handle it carefully as his teacher.

grounding: An elder recalls a teen crush on a teacher, keeping it private rather than giving her a dramatic note, and how it passed.
